metadata.description: Name of the Log Analytics workspace that Microsoft Sentinel is enabled on.

properties.displayName: Password spray from a single IP address
properties.description:
One IP address failed to sign in to many different accounts within an hour: wrong password (error 50126), smart lockout (50053) or an account name that does not exist (50034). Trying a few common passwords against many accounts is a password spray; a user who forgot a password fails many times on one account instead. The alert also says whether any of the accounts that failed went on to sign in successfully from the same address.

False positives: A shared egress address (office NAT, VPN, proxy) after a password-expiry wave or an outage that forces everyone to sign in again; some of those users will also show as successful, because they mistyped and then got it right. A misconfigured application with stale credentials fails on one account many times and does not reach the account threshold.

Response: Start with the accounts listed in SuccessfulAccounts: if the address is not yours, treat them as compromised, revoke sessions, reset the passwords and review their activity. Block the address and confirm smart lockout and the banned-password list are enabled.

MITRE ATT&CK sub-techniques: T1110.003.

Source: SentinelWork rule ID-001.
properties.query:
let MinAccounts = 15;
let ExcludedIPs = dynamic([]);
let Failed = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
    | where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
    | where ResultType in ("50126", "50053", "50034")
    | where IPAddress !in (ExcludedIPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, IPAddress, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, UserAgent, Location;
let Sprays = Failed
    | summarize FailedAttempts = count(),
                TargetAccounts = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
                AccountSample = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 25),
                Applications = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10),
                UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5),
                Country = take_any(Location),
                FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
                LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
                by IPAddress
    | where TargetAccounts >= MinAccounts;
let Guessed = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
    | where ResultType == "0"
    | join kind=inner (Failed | distinct IPAddress, UserPrincipalName) on IPAddress, UserPrincipalName
    | summarize SuccessCount = count(), SuccessfulAccounts = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 25) by IPAddress;
Sprays
| join kind=leftouter Guessed on IPAddress
| extend SuccessfulSignIns = coalesce(SuccessCount, 0)
| extend Outcome = iff(SuccessfulSignIns > 0, "At least one targeted account also signed in from the address", "No targeted account signed in from the address")
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, IPAddress, Country, TargetAccounts, FailedAttempts, SuccessfulSignIns,
          SuccessfulAccounts, Outcome, AccountSample, Applications, UserAgents

properties.displayName: Repeated MFA denials followed by a successful sign-in
properties.description:
A user's multifactor prompt failed or was denied several times (error 500121) and, within the hour after those denials, a sign-in that required MFA succeeded. That is the shape of MFA fatigue: an attacker who already has the password sends prompts until the user approves one. Only denials before the successful sign-in are counted.

False positives: A user who mistypes a code or ignores prompts on a new phone and then gets it right. Those cases usually show one address and one device throughout.

Response: Call the user on a known number. If they did not start the sign-ins, revoke sessions, reset the password, review MFA methods registered in the last days and check what the session did after SuccessTime.

Source: SentinelWork rule ID-002.
properties.query:
let MinDenials = 5;
let Denials = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(3h)
    | where ResultType == "500121"
    | project UserId, DenialTime = TimeGenerated, DenialAddress = IPAddress, DenialReason = ResultDescription;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
| where ResultType == "0" and AuthenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication"
| project SuccessTime = TimeGenerated, UserId, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Country = Location,
          Application = AppDisplayName
| join kind=inner Denials on UserId
| where DenialTime < SuccessTime and DenialTime > SuccessTime - 1h
| summarize MfaDenials = count(),
            FirstDenial = min(DenialTime),
            LastDenial = max(DenialTime),
            DenialAddresses = make_set(DenialAddress, 10),
            DenialReasons = make_set(DenialReason, 5)
            by UserId, UserPrincipalName, SuccessTime, IPAddress, Country, Application
| where MfaDenials >= MinDenials
| summarize arg_min(SuccessTime, *) by UserId
| project SuccessTime, UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress, Country, Application, MfaDenials, FirstDenial,
          LastDenial, DenialAddresses, DenialReasons

properties.displayName: Successful sign-in from a country new for the user
properties.description:
A user signed in successfully from a country that none of their successful sign-ins came from in the previous 14 days. Users with no sign-in history in that time are left out, so a new starter does not alert on their first day.

False positives: Business travel and holidays; a VPN or mobile carrier that exits in another country; a user who has not signed in for more than 14 days.

Response: Check the device, application and whether MFA was satisfied. Ask the user. If they are not travelling, revoke sessions and reset the password.

MITRE ATT&CK sub-techniques: T1078.004.

Source: SentinelWork rule ID-003.
properties.query:
let ExpectedCountries = dynamic([]);
let Known = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(14d) .. ago(2h))
    | where ResultType == "0" and isnotempty(Location)
    | summarize by UserId, Location;
let History = Known
    | summarize KnownCountries = strcat_array(make_set(Location, 20), ", ") by UserId;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
| where ResultType == "0" and isnotempty(Location)
| where Location !in (ExpectedCountries)
| join kind=leftanti Known on UserId, Location
| join kind=inner History on UserId
| summarize SignIns = count(),
            Applications = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10),
            arg_min(TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, KnownCountries, UserAgent)
            by UserId, NewCountry = Location
| project FirstSeen = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress, NewCountry, KnownCountries, SignIns,
          Applications, UserAgent

properties.description:
An account signed in successfully with a legacy protocol such as IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH or Exchange ActiveSync. These protocols cannot do MFA, so a stolen password is all an attacker needs, which is why password sprays aim at them. Both interactive and non-interactive sign-ins are read; if the non-interactive table is not collected, the rule still runs on the other.

False positives: Printers and scanners that send mail with SMTP AUTH, old mail clients, and line of business applications that have not moved to modern authentication.

Response: Confirm the device and address belong to the user. If not, reset the password and revoke sessions. Either way, move the account off the legacy protocol.

MITRE ATT&CK sub-techniques: T1078.004.

Source: SentinelWork rule ID-004.
properties.query:
let AllowedAccounts = dynamic([]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (SigninLogs
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
     | where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
     | where ResultType == "0"
     | project TimeGenerated, ClientAppUsed, UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, Location,
               SignInType = "Interactive"),
    (AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
     | where ingestion_time() > ago(1h)
     | where ResultType == "0"
     | project TimeGenerated, ClientAppUsed, UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, Location,
               SignInType = "Non-interactive")
| where isnotempty(ClientAppUsed) and ClientAppUsed !in ("Browser", "Mobile Apps and Desktop clients")
| where UserPrincipalName !in~ (AllowedAccounts)
| summarize SignIns = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Protocols = strcat_array(make_set(ClientAppUsed, 10), ", "),
            SignInTypes = strcat_array(make_set(SignInType, 2), ", "),
            Applications = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10),
            Country = take_any(Location)
            by UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, UserPrincipalName, UserId, IPAddress, Country, Protocols, SignInTypes, SignIns,
          Applications
